text: Fat-rich diet not only affects individuals who consume it, but it can also impact their offspring, leading to inherited metabolic disruption and potentially modifying behavior. Behavioral changes may favor a preference for palatable foods and the emergence of anxiety-like behaviors. This study aimed to evaluate the preference for palatable food, food-seeking, and anxiety behaviors in the offspring (F1) of parents that consumed a high-fat diet (F0).
source_label: Sex-dependent phenotypes of anxiety and palatable food-seeking in offspring born from rats exposed to a high-fat diet
